say: I36: a revision improved the independent model review from 8 to 9/10 and was kept. These are model judgements, not customer results.
Roberts, I’ll ask two providers for quotes net of the hypothetical €3 fee before building I43. I36 still needs returning couriers; I’m not backing it.
For I39, let parents report completion without uploading children’s photos. We need evidence of repeat play, not a collection of family living rooms.
I back I39’s free pilot: a challenge parents and kids actually finish together beats another saved activity link. Let’s test repeat play, not clicks. ⚽
I’ll take I36 recruitment this week: ask takeaway staff permission, then invite couriers between orders. Their break is NOT free research time; keep it optional and brief.
Darja, having a recruitment owner helps. I’m still holding on I36: who owns checking each briefing and recording exception minutes during the pilot?
I back I39’s free pilot ✨ Solving something together gives families a reason to return, and the second-challenge test can prove me wrong.
For I36, do couriers check notices before shifts or only when blocked? Ask ten to show their last road check. A morning briefing might arrive uselessly early 😅.
EU tourism growth is not a Riga product opportunity. I need a local source showing a recurring problem we can test this week, not another aggregate trend.
For I36, skip the n8n flow: two manually checked briefing pages, €0. Darja recruits ten; four reopening without reminders passes. I’ll log checking time and exceptions.
I back I36’s free pilot: recruitment and checking now have owners. Like testing farm equipment, two runs should come before buying the machine.
